law: the pressure of the air upon a moving surface is fixed by Smeaton's coefficient of .005, used by engineers since 1759 and adopted in the tables of Lilienthal
plain: the pressure of the air upon a moving surface is fixed by a coefficient of .005
obs: two brothers building gliders by these tables find their machines give scarcely two-thirds of the lift computed, and small surfaces tried in a wind-trunk show the same deficiency

law: light is a wave spread continuously through space, as Young, Fresnel and Maxwell established, so that it delivers its energy in proportion to its brightness
plain: light delivers its energy continuously, in proportion to its brightness
obs: when light falls upon a clean metal plate, the swiftness of the electrified particles driven off depends on the colour of the light alone and not on its brightness, and feeble violet light drives them off at once while the strongest red light drives off none

law: light is borne by a stationary luminiferous ether through which the earth moves, as Fresnel, Maxwell and Lord Kelvin hold, so that its speed measured on the earth differs along and across the earth's motion
plain: light is borne by a stationary medium through which the earth moves, so that its speed measured on the earth differs along and across the earth's motion
obs: the most delicate interferometer, turned in every direction and tried at every season, shows no difference whatever in the speed of light along and across the earth's motion

law: Newton's law of universal gravitation, by the inverse square of the distance, governs exactly the motions of all the planets
plain: attraction by the inverse square of the distance governs exactly the motions of all the planets
obs: the perihelion of Mercury advances forty-three seconds of arc in a century more than all the known planets can account for, and sixty years of search have found no body within its orbit

law: the atoms of the chemical elements are immutable, as Dalton taught and all chemistry since Lavoisier confirms, so that no element can change into another
plain: no chemical element can change into another
obs: a preparation of thorium, freed of every impurity, continually produces a new substance of different chemical character, which in turn gives rise to a gas, and the production can be neither hastened nor stayed by heat or any reagent

law: the atoms of all solid elements have the same capacity for heat at every temperature, the law of Dulong and Petit
plain: the atoms of all solid elements have the same capacity for heat at every temperature
obs: diamond, and other solids cooled toward the greatest cold attainable, take up far less heat than the law requires, the capacity falling toward nothing as the temperature falls

law: the continents and ocean basins have kept their places since the crust first hardened, as Lyell, Dana and the whole body of geologists teach
plain: the continents and ocean basins have kept their places since the crust first hardened
obs: the coasts of Africa and South America fit one another like the edges of torn paper, the same rock formations and the same fossil reptiles and plants lie on the two sides, and the marks of ancient glaciers are found in lands now tropical

law: the blood of all healthy men is alike, as the physiologists teach, so that the blood of one may be mingled with that of another without change
plain: the blood of all healthy men is alike, so that the blood of one may be mingled with that of another without change
obs: when the serum of one healthy man is mixed with the red corpuscles of another, in many pairs the corpuscles clump together and in other pairs they do not, the result being constant for each pair of persons

law: a diet of pure proteids, fats, carbohydrates and salts suffices for health, as Liebig and Voit established, and a disease that spreads through a ship or barracks is the work of a germ, as Koch has shown
plain: a diet of pure proteids, fats, carbohydrates and salts suffices for health, and a disease that spreads through a ship or barracks is the work of a germ
obs: fowls and men fed on polished rice fall into the palsy called beri-beri and recover when given the polishings of the rice, though no microbe is found and the disease cannot be conveyed from the sick to the well

law: all the atoms of one element are exactly alike in weight, as Dalton laid down
plain: all the atoms of one element are exactly alike in weight
obs: lead taken from uranium minerals and lead taken from thorium minerals, purified with every care and chemically inseparable, differ constantly in atomic weight

law: the properties of the elements are a periodic function of their atomic weights, as Mendeleeff's law declares
plain: the properties of the elements follow the order of their atomic weights
obs: tellurium is heavier than iodine, and argon heavier than potassium, by the most exact determinations repeated over many years, yet their properties demand the contrary order

law: a rocket is driven by the pressure of its gases against the air behind it, as is everywhere taught, so that in a vacuum it could gain no speed
plain: a rocket is driven by the pressure of its gases against the air behind it, so that in a vacuum it could gain no speed
obs: a rocket fired within a vessel exhausted of air recoils more strongly than the same rocket fired in the open air

law: the Milky Way comprises the whole sidereal universe, and the spiral nebulae are clouds within it, as Huggins and the best authorities hold
plain: the Milky Way comprises the whole sidereal universe, and the spiral nebulae are clouds within it
obs: in the great nebula of Andromeda single stars are made out which vary in light exactly as certain stars near us do, and from their faintness they lie many times farther off than the remotest part of the Milky Way

law: the universe of stars is at rest as a whole, neither spreading nor shrinking, as Newton held and all astronomers assume
plain: the universe of stars is at rest as a whole, neither spreading nor shrinking
obs: the lines in the spectra of the distant nebulae are all displaced toward the red, and the more so in proportion as the nebula is fainter and farther off

law: the cathode rays consist of minute particles of matter carrying electricity, as J. J. Thomson proved by weighing them
plain: the cathode rays consist of minute particles of matter carrying electricity
obs: a stream of these particles reflected from a crystal of nickel, or passed through thin metal foil, forms rings and bands of the very kind that waves form, with a spacing that depends on the speed of the particles

law: the pancreas is roused to secrete solely through the nerves, as Pawlow has shown for all the digestive glands
plain: the pancreas is roused to secrete solely through the nerves
obs: when every nerve to the bowel and pancreas has been cut, acid placed in the bowel still calls forth the pancreatic juice, and an extract of the bowel lining injected into the blood does the same

law: the nerve acts upon the heart and the muscles by the electric current alone, as du Bois-Reymond established
plain: the nerve acts upon the heart and the muscles by the electric current alone
obs: when the nerve that slows a frog's heart is excited, and the fluid bathing that heart is carried over to a second heart which has no nerves, the second heart slows likewise

law: rubber, starch and cellulose are loose clusters of small molecules, since, as the chemists agree, no single molecule can exceed a few thousand in weight
plain: rubber, starch and cellulose are loose clusters of small molecules, no single molecule exceeding a few thousand in weight
obs: rubber changed chemically by the addition of hydrogen, so that the forces supposed to bind the clusters are removed, keeps its great apparent molecular weight and its viscous character unaltered

law: a disease that seizes many persons together in asylums and villages is conveyed by a germ, according to the doctrine of Pasteur and Koch
plain: a disease that seizes many persons together in asylums and villages is conveyed by a germ
obs: in asylums where pellagra rages among the inmates, the nurses and attendants who live among them never take it, and inmates given fresh meat and milk recover while the rest do not

law: a ray of light passing the sun is bent, if at all, by no more than the small amount which Newton's law of gravitation assigns to a swift corpuscle
plain: a ray of light passing the sun is bent, if at all, by no more than a certain small amount computed from the attraction of gravity
obs: stars photographed close to the sun's edge during a total eclipse, at two stations far apart, are displaced outward by twice that amount

law: the energy of heat is shared equally among all the modes of vibration of a body, by the theorem of Maxwell and Boltzmann
plain: the energy of heat is shared equally among all the modes of vibration of a body
obs: the radiation within a heated enclosure contains almost no energy in the shortest waves, whereas the theorem demands that nearly all the energy lie there and that the total be without limit

law: yellow fever is conveyed by the clothing and bedding of the sick, against which every port enforces quarantine and disinfection by the advice of the sanitary authorities
plain: yellow fever is conveyed by the clothing and bedding of the sick
obs: volunteers who sleep for weeks in the soiled bedding of those dead of the fever remain well, while others kept in a clean house, and bitten by mosquitoes that had fed upon the sick, take the fever

law: no machine heavier than the air can sustain itself and carry a man in flight with any engine known, as Professor Newcomb has demonstrated and Lord Kelvin affirms
plain: no machine heavier than the air can sustain itself and carry a man in flight with any engine known
obs: a machine weighing with its rider seven hundred pounds, driven by a petrol engine of twelve horse-power, is reported by five witnesses to have risen from level ground and flown eight hundred and fifty feet against the wind

law: the coelacanth fishes perished with the great reptiles, as the palaeontologists agree, no trace of them being found in any later rock
plain: the coelacanth fishes perished with the great reptiles, no trace of them being found in any later rock
obs: a fish five feet long, having the lobed fins and every bony character of that family, is taken alive in a trawl off the coast of South Africa

law: energy is never created nor destroyed, the principle of Mayer, Joule and Helmholtz
plain: energy is never created nor destroyed
obs: when certain radio-active atoms cast out an electrified particle, the particles from like atoms carry off unequal energies, and the remainder is nowhere to be found by the most careful calorimeter

law: an invisible ray that leaves no trace upon a photographic plate or any instrument cannot be sorted by a prism, according to the laws of optics from Newton to Kirchhoff
plain: an invisible ray that leaves no trace upon a photographic plate or any instrument cannot be sorted by a prism
obs: a professor of physics at Nancy reports that a new ray from heated metals, sorted by a prism of aluminium, brightens a feeble spark as judged by his eye in a darkened room, and several of his colleagues report the same

law: the power of reckoning with numbers belongs to man alone among animals, as naturalists from Aristotle onward have held
plain: the power of reckoning with numbers belongs to man alone among animals
obs: a horse in Berlin taps out with his hoof the correct answers to sums set him, before a committee of learned men, and even when his master is absent

law: the electric waves travel in straight lines as light does, as Hertz proved
plain: the electric waves travel in straight lines as light does
obs: signals sent from Cornwall are received in Newfoundland, though the bulge of the ocean rises more than a hundred miles between the two stations

law: heat cannot arise of itself without chemical change or the expenditure of work, by the first law of thermodynamics
plain: heat cannot arise of itself without chemical change or the expenditure of work
obs: a salt of radium keeps itself always warmer than its surroundings, giving out heat enough to melt more than its own weight of ice every hour, month after month, with no chemical change that can be detected

law: living things arise only from living things, as Pasteur and Tyndall proved
plain: living things arise only from living things
obs: a physician of London reports that sealed tubes of saline solutions, heated above the boiling point, show after some months minute moving bodies under the microscope

law: characters acquired during life are not inherited, as Weismann has shown
plain: characters acquired during life are not inherited
obs: a naturalist of Vienna reports that toads compelled to breed in water for several generations bear young having the dark swollen pads upon the hand that belong to the water-breeding kinds

law: Newton's law of universal gravitation, by the inverse square of the distance, governs exactly the motions of all the planets
plain: attraction by the inverse square of the distance governs exactly the motions of all the planets
obs: the planet Uranus, after full allowance for Neptune, is found by some computers still to depart from its tables by a small quantity
